title: Mahabharata
author: Vyasa
description: Ancient Indian epic of the Kurukshetra War and the fates of the Kaurava and Pandava princes
significance: One of the longest epic poems ever composed; foundational text of Hindu philosophy

title: Ramayana
author: Valmiki
description: Epic poem narrating the life of Prince Rama and his quest to rescue his wife Sita
significance: Foundational epic of Indian civilization; influenced literature across Southeast Asia

title: Iliad
author: Homer
description: Epic poem set during the Trojan War, focusing on the wrath of Achilles
significance: Foundation of Western literature; established conventions of the epic genre

title: Odyssey
author: Homer
description: Epic poem following Odysseus's journey home after the Trojan War
significance: Archetypal journey narrative; foundation of Western storytelling

title: Oedipus Rex
author: Sophocles
description: Tragedy of King Oedipus who fulfills a prophecy that he would kill his father and marry his mother
significance: Considered the perfect tragedy by Aristotle; foundational work of dramatic irony

title: Aeneid
author: Virgil
description: Epic poem telling the story of Aeneas's journey from Troy to Italy
significance: Rome's national epic; bridge between Greek and Latin literary traditions

title: Metamorphoses
author: Ovid
description: Mythological narrative poem covering transformations from the creation of the world to Julius Caesar
significance: Most influential source of classical mythology in Western literature

title: Journey to the West
author: Wu Cheng'en
description: Novel following the monk Xuanzang's pilgrimage to obtain Buddhist sutras, accompanied by Sun Wukong
significance: One of the Four Great Classical Novels of Chinese literature

title: Dream of the Red Chamber
author: Cao Xueqin
description: Novel depicting the rise and decline of a great aristocratic family during the Qing dynasty
significance: Considered the greatest Chinese novel; pinnacle of Chinese fiction

title: The Mu'allaqat
author: Various
description: Collection of seven pre-Islamic Arabic poems considered the finest of their era
significance: Foundational works of Arabic literary tradition; hung in the Kaaba

title: One Thousand and One Nights
author: Various
description: Collection of tales told by Scheherazade to delay her execution
significance: One of the most influential works of world literature; introduced frame narrative

title: The Tale of Genji
author: Murasaki Shikibu
description: Narrative of the life of Hikaru Genji, son of an ancient Japanese emperor
significance: Often considered the world's first novel; masterwork of Japanese prose

title: The Pillow Book
author: Sei Shonagon
description: Collection of observations, lists, and reflections by a court lady during the Heian period
significance: Pioneered the zuihitsu (essay) genre; vivid portrait of Heian court life

title: Beowulf
author: Anonymous
description: Epic poem about the hero Beowulf's battles against monsters Grendel and a dragon
significance: Longest surviving Old English poem; cornerstone of English literary heritage

title: Shahnameh
author: Ferdowsi
description: Epic poem recounting the mythical and historical past of the Persian Empire
significance: National epic of Iran; preserved Persian language and identity

title: Masnavi
author: Rumi
description: Six-volume poem of spiritual teaching through stories and allegories
significance: One of the most influential works of Sufi literature; widely read globally

title: Divine Comedy
author: Dante Alighieri
description: Epic poem describing the author's journey through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise
significance: Established Italian as a literary language; pinnacle of medieval literature

title: Canterbury Tales
author: Geoffrey Chaucer
description: Collection of stories told by pilgrims on their way to Canterbury Cathedral
significance: Established English as a literary language; vivid portrait of medieval society

title: Tirukkural
author: Thiruvalluvar
description: Collection of 1,330 couplets covering virtue, wealth, and love
significance: Foundational Tamil text; translated into over 40 languages

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
description: Epic novel interweaving the stories of five aristocratic families during the Napoleonic Wars
significance: Often called the greatest novel ever written; redefined the scope of the novel

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: Philosophical novel about the moral struggles of three brothers after their father's murder
significance: Considered a pinnacle of world literature; profound exploration of faith and doubt

title: Epic of Sundiata
author: Griots
description: Epic of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire, transmitted orally by griots
significance: Foundational narrative of the Mandé peoples; exemplar of oral epic tradition
